3.0.s.en: (1) Rebuking the Galatians for clinging to the works of the Law

3.0.0.en: Foolish: Paul rebukes the Galatians for their great ignorance in believing that the Law is the cause of their salvation, so that they clung to it after they were baptized. Paul does not break the commandment by saying "foolish", because he is their teacher and their father, responsible for them, and he rebukes them over the most important matter in their lives, which is their salvation, but he kept his peace and was not angry.

3.0.1.en: Bewitched you: that is, enchanted you, from the incantation used in sorcery; it means that he changed you completely, to this degree, away from the right faith.

3.0.3.en: The truth: the faith, because Christ alone is the Savior and not the works of the Law.

3.0.4.en: Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you: in the ancient Greek original in which the Holy Bible was written, it means picturing the crucified Christ in the mind.

3.0.5.en: The Apostle rebukes the Galatians for leaving faith in Christ the Savior and returning to reliance on the Law as a source of salvation.

3.1.0.en: The hearing of faith: the preaching and proclaiming of Christ the Savior that Paul delivered among them. Paul asks the Galatians, in astonishment, about the cause of the blessings in which they live, which is the work of the Holy Spirit in them with all His gifts and fruits: is it the works of the Law or their faith in Christ the Savior? Of course the answer is that the Holy Spirit and all His gifts are grace which they receive by faith.

3.2.0.en: Man is supposed to grow spiritually, but they began with faith and went back to the fleshly ordinances of the Law such as circumcision.

3.3.0.en: Your endurance of sufferings and persecutions for the sake of Christ was not in vain; what is in vain is the attempt to reach perfection by the works of the Law.

3.4.0.en: Paul repeats the question so that they may examine themselves: did they attain these gifts and powers because of their commitment to the Law or by the power of faith? ... Paul was always urging steadfastness in faith: "Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him" (Heb 10:38), "work out your own salvation with fear and trembling" (Phil 2:12). Perhaps this passage answers those who say that a believer cannot fall away. For these fell away after they had believed, because they listened to the false teachers.

3.4.1.en: Let us constantly examine ourselves: is our spiritual life advancing or declining?! If we notice a decline, we look for the cause, which may be negligence toward a certain sin or shortcoming in our prayers and readings, and repentance and confession bring us back again to the way of the Kingdom.

3.5.s.en: (2) Abraham, the example of justification by faith

3.5.0.en: The Apostle Paul presents proofs from Scripture, taking Abraham, the father of the Jewish people, as an example that justification is by faith and not by the works of the Law. For Abraham believed, and his faith was counted as righteousness, and this was before the Law of Moses and before circumcision (Gen 15:6).

3.6.0.en: The Apostle affirms that belonging to Abraham is according to the active faith of Abraham and not according to physical descent, and therefore the Lord Christ said to them, "If ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the works of Abraham" (Jn 8:39). And because God had foreseen that the Gentiles would believe in Christ, He promised Abraham, "in thy seed (Christ) shall all the nations of the earth be blessed" (Gen 26:4). So whoever walks in the way of Abraham in faith receives the promise of blessing. Abraham's faith was practical, for he left everything and obeyed and offered his only son Isaac, so God said to him, "By myself have I sworn, saith the LORD, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son: That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore" (Gen 22:16, 17). So the work here is the work of grace in man's life as a result of living faith, and there is no place for the Law in God's promise to Abraham.

3.6.1.en: Let us have practical faith in our lives, so that we bring God into all our works and trust in His supporting power, and are not troubled by tribulations, for He is able to bring us through them and we come out stronger.

3.7.s.en: (3) A comparison between the Law and faith

3.7.0.en: Whoever lives by the Law will not be able to fulfill everything in it, and so he becomes deficient and cursed, because he sinned by not fulfilling the Law. The book of Deuteronomy affirms this (Deut 27:26), and this verse is cited here to declare the necessity of fulfilling the whole Law, or else man becomes cursed.

3.8.0.en: Justification, then, will not be by the Law, which curses everyone who falls short in one point of it, but by faith, as the prophet Habakkuk mentions in his prophecy (Hab 2:4).

3.9.0.en: The difference between faith and the works of the Law is clear. The latter does not justify the one who neglects them, and there is no one who can live by all the demands of the Law, so life and justification are by faith, while the Law prepared the way for faith in Christ.

3.10.0.en: Christ fulfilled the Law for us, for He alone was able to do so, and He was crucified for us. Crucifixion is the sign of shame and of the curse, that is, Christ the Righteous became a curse for us in order to remove from us the curse and the need to fulfill the Law. He fulfilled it for us so that we might believe in Him and receive justification, and no longer need to fulfill the works of the Law.

3.11.0.en: Thus it appears that justification is by faith and not by the works of the Law. Not only the Jews who believe, but the Gentiles also, so that all receive justification in Christ and the work of the Holy Spirit with all His gifts and fruits overflows upon them.

3.11.1.en: If salvation is available to us when we believe in Christ, let us no longer rely on our own ideas or on our abilities apart from God, but trust in Christ and rely on Him in everything, to open the way for the work of the Holy Spirit in us.

3.12.s.en: (4) The Law does not annul the promises

3.12.0.en: Brethren: because they are believers and members of the one body of Christ.

3.12.1.en: After the manner of men: that is, by human reasoning.

3.12.3.en: It is well known that any promise made by any man remains firm, and no one can take anything from it or add anything to it. How much more, then, if the promise is from God, it remains firm.

3.13.0.en: The divine promises were made to Abraham, and of course they remain firm and no one can break them. God promised Abraham and said "to thy seed" and not "to seeds". So what is meant is one person and not a group, and this person is Christ, who came from the seed of Abraham and offers salvation to the whole world, so that the whole world that believes in Him is blessed in Him.

3.14.1.en: Paul declares that the Law, which was given to Moses about 430 years after God's promise to Abraham, cannot abolish God's promises. The promises are salvation by Christ the Redeemer, so the Law cannot abolish them and be a substitute for them in man's salvation; rather, the Law is merely the preparer of the way for faith in Christ.

3.15.0.en: The inheritance of salvation is not by the Law but by God's promise which He gave to Abraham and which is fulfilled in Christ. If salvation were by the Law, then it would not be by God's promise to Abraham, that is, salvation would not be by Christ. Of course the Jews do not accept the abolition of the divine promise to Abraham, which is fulfilled only in Christ. So salvation and justification are by Christ and not by the Law, because the inheritance by the Law is considered a wage for the one who fulfills it, whereas the inheritance by the divine promise is a free gift, and these two are opposites. So Paul affirms that God gave the inheritance to Abraham by promise and not by the works of the Law, and this promise is fulfilled through salvation in Christ, while the Law made known to us sin and its penalty, that is, it was a preparation for Christ, in whom we believe, so that He saves us from its penalty and we live with Him and in Him the new life.

3.16.1.en: Transgressions: the many sins into which man fell after God's promise to Abraham.

3.16.3.en: Angels: those who gave Moses the Law.

3.16.5.en: The Apostle Paul poses a question and answers it: since the Law did not justify us, why did God give it after His promise to Abraham? The answer is that people did not walk according to the faith of our father Abraham, so God laid down for them the statutes of the Law like a bridle that restrains them so that they do not slip into evil, and to lead them in carrying out the commandment, so He made known to them sin and its penalty. But until when?.. Until Christ comes, and when He comes the mission of the Law ends. And the Apostle Paul declares that the Law, according to the inherited Jewish tradition, was given by God to Moses by means of angels, to deliver it and explain it to Moses, as St. Stephen indicated: "Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it" (Acts 7:53).

3.17.0.en: Is not a mediator of one: mediation is always between two, and the Law is a mediator between two, who are God and man.

3.17.1.en: But God is one: He is the One who gave the promise as a free gift without the intervention of man, and this promise is fulfilled in Christ the Savior. So salvation is by Christ and not by the Law.

3.17.2.en: The mediator is between two parties, and Moses himself can be considered a mediator who carried God's Law to the people. The Law did not depend only on the giver of the commandment but also on man's keeping of the Law, because it is a covenant between two, but he failed.

3.17.3.en: There is no contradiction between this verse and the speaking of Christ as the mediator for reconciling man with God (1 Tim 2:5), because Christ, since the Law failed in its mediation between God and man, came incarnate and as the Redeemer of man to fulfill the divine promise given to Abraham.

3.18.0.en: Paul strongly denies that the Law which God gave is against His promises, because the Law, as we mentioned, reveals sin and its penalty, that is, it alerts man to it so that he rejects it. But man alone is unable to repent and be rid of sin, and he needs Christ the Savior, who rescues him and gives him life.

3.18.1.en: Therefore the Law is unable to give man the new life, because it does not save him from sin and does not justify him.

3.19.0.en: The scripture: the books of the Holy Bible, especially the legislation, that is, the Law.

3.19.1.en: Concluded: it showed the weakness of all people and their deserving of judgment and eternal death because of their sins. The Law condemned all people and sentenced them to death because of their sins, their transgressions of it and their shortcomings, and by this it prepared for the work of Christ, who saves man from the prison of sin and gives him new life (1 Pet 3:19).

3.20.0.en: Paul makes clear that before the Incarnation of Christ the people of God were under the guard of the Law, which alerted them to sin so that they tried to keep away from it, and consequently they were better than the pagans who made light of sin. So the people of God differed in their character and customs from the rest of the peoples, since the Law kept them and shut them in so that they would not go astray by treating sin as permissible. But they were unable to fulfill the whole Law, so they were sentenced to death and shut up in the prison of sin until Christ came and freed them from it by His redemption. So the Law kept the people of God until, in the fullness of time, faith in Christ the Savior would be revealed.

3.21.0.en: The Apostle Paul shows the work of the Law not only in keeping the people of God but also in disciplining them. As a tutor or instructor, it showed the wrongs so that people would keep away from them, but it did not save them, so they understood truth from falsehood and felt their need for the salvation that was accomplished by Christ.

3.22.0.en: Therefore, after faith in Christ, who gives us the ability to leave sin and moves us to the new, pure life, we do not need the Law, whose work ended with the coming of Christ.

3.22.1.en: Accept warning and rebuke from others and take refuge in God, who gives you by the Holy Spirit repentance and new life in His Church. And be submissive to the work of the Holy Spirit in you, who always guides you to life with God.

3.23.0.en: The Apostle Paul declares that all who believe in Christ have become sons of God and not slaves, because they were born again in Baptism and so became sons of God and put on a new nature which Christ the Savior gave them, and became members united with the body of Christ, that is, the Church. In faith all human distinctions have ended, such as a man's being Jewish by origin or Greek, that is, a Gentile who is not a Jew, and He also ended the difference between slaves and free, since He raised all to the rank of sonship to God by Baptism. Likewise the ancient peoples, and some religions until now, regarded woman as lower than man, but he declared that male and female have become in one standing, that is, sons of God by Baptism, and have put on Christ, that is, the new nature. So all Christians are one before God, regardless of differences of origin, social standing, sex or any other differences.

3.24.0.en: Paul reaches the final conclusion, which is that faith in Christ is the fulfillment of God's promises to Abraham, so the believers become children of Abraham and heirs of the Kingdom. This spiritual sonship by faith and Baptism is the true sonship, and not the physical sonship that the Jews imagined for themselves and boasted of.

3.24.1.en: Contemplate the grace you enjoy, which you received by Baptism, which is the new nature inclined to become like God. And if by Baptism you have put on Christ, do not act except according to His will, so that you are a living image of Him that draws people to Him and does not cause them to stumble. Thus you will be walking with steady steps on the way of the Kingdom. Sons and heirs

4.0.0.en: The heir: signifies the believers in the Old Testament.

4.0.1.en: Tutors (guardians): the guardian is the one who, by law, has charge of the minor child so that he does not reach out for the inheritance before the age of maturity. The guardian here signifies the Law.

4.0.2.en: Governors (stewards): the steward is the one appointed by the guardian to look after the child's affairs in his living, health and education, and here he signifies the ordinances of the Law and its rulings.

4.0.3.en: The time appointed: the time of the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption.

4.0.4.en: The elements of the world: that is, the material ordinances of the Law such as purifications and washings.

4.0.5.en: The believers in the Old Testament were subject to the commandments of the Law and its material rulings, and strove by them to fulfill it, but they failed and were unable to be freed from the yoke of bondage to sin so as to enjoy their rights as sons. So they were in the condition of slaves, awaiting the Messiah the Savior to set them free, like minor children for whom the time has not come to act freely in their inheritance, that is, their sonship to God which they receive in the Christian life.

4.0.6.en: God has given us a very special boldness toward Him so that we may enjoy His fatherhood and speak to Him about our life, our circumstances and our hopes. Do we use it?

4.1.0.en: The fulness of the time: the time of the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption.

4.1.2.en: Under the law: that is, He was born a Jew subject to the Law.

4.1.3.en: The eternal Son became incarnate of the Virgin to take our human nature, and was born as a Jew to fulfill the Law on behalf of man, who was unable to fulfill it, and then to die without any sin that He had committed, in order to take away our sins and redeem all people who are unable to fulfill the Law. Since He fulfilled it for us and died for our redemption, He gave us sonship to Him, so we became sons by adoption. This, of course, is different from the Son's sonship in essence from eternity with the Father.

4.1.4.en: He was born of a woman and took our human nature so that He could redeem mankind, and because He is God, the Infinite, His sacrifice is able to forgive all the sins of the world, which are infinite and directed against the infinite God.

4.2.0.en: The Spirit of his Son: the Holy Spirit.

4.2.3.en: Since in the New Testament we receive sonship to God through Baptism, we become qualified for the work of the Holy Spirit of God in us, who gives us the boldness of sonship and teaches us how to pray and feel God's fatherhood, so that we call Him "Papa, Father." Paul mentioned it in both languages to confirm the meaning of sonship.

4.3.0.en: Thus the believer moves from the bondage of sin, which the Law reveals, to sonship to God by faith and Baptism, and by this sonship the Kingdom of Heaven awaits him as a reward from Christ, if he stays firm in his sonship to God throughout his life.

4.3.1.en: Your sonship to God opens wide horizons for you in your relationship with Him. It gives you reassurance, a striving to become like Him, and an inclination to be with Him, so that you experience Him not only in prayers and readings and in union in the sacrament of the Eucharist, but also behold Him and feel Him with you in all your steps, until you enjoy being with Him forever in heaven.

4.4.s.en: (2) Returning to the Law after faith

4.4.0.en: Which by nature are no gods: that is, the idols.

4.4.1.en: Are known of God: that is, God loved you, accepted you and redeemed you.

4.4.2.en: Weak elements: the fleshly commandments of the Law such as circumcision.

4.4.3.en: Beggarly: that is, empty of grace, relying on failing human effort.

4.4.4.en: Paul reminds the Galatians that they were far from God and worshiped idols, but they believed in Christ and He accepted them and saved them from their sins. How then do they return to reliance on the Law, which does not save its followers, because there is no grace of God in it, but it is merely a revealing of sin and its hideousness?

4.4.5.en: Thank God for His care for you and for the salvation offered to you on the altar every day as true Body and Blood, and ask His help in all your steps, and He will support you and you will succeed in all your works.

4.5.0.en: Days, and months, and times, and years: the times that the Law set for worship and feasts.

4.5.1.en: Bestowed upon you labour: I preached to you.

4.5.2.en: The Apostle Paul is astonished at the Galatians' clinging to the Law as the foundation of their salvation, so that he declares his fear for them, that they did not understand his message about Christ and laid a foundation for salvation other than His blood shed for them. Of course this is different from the Church's concern for feasts and fasts, because they are an expression of love and spiritual remembrances resulting from faith in Christ and not a foundation for obtaining salvation. They are necessary expressions for every true believer who loves Christ, so that he does not forget Him amid the preoccupations of life.

4.6.s.en: (3) Reminding the Galatians of their first love

4.6.0.en: Be as I am: in my faith in the blood of Christ the Savior alone.

4.6.1.en: For I am as ye are: I do not cling to the distinction and rights of the Jews but live as one of the Gentiles.

4.6.2.en: Ye have not injured me at all: you were kind in your treatment of me when I visited you, and you honored me.

4.6.3.en: Paul spoke with kindness and humility to the Galatians, and entreats them to believe as he does that salvation is by the blood of Christ alone and not by the Law, because their sonship to him and their love lead them to follow his example. His fatherhood also made him deal with them as one of them, and he did not boast of his advantages as a Jew from the people of God and better than the pagan Gentiles. Then he reminds them of their kindness in dealing with him when he visited them and preached to them, and of their first love for him, and calls them to return to their sonship to him and not to follow the false teachings of the teachers of Jewish origin who turn against him and his teachings.

4.7.0.en: Infirmity of the flesh: Paul's bodily weakness, which was most likely the weakness of his eyesight and sores on his body that he used to bind with pieces of cloth.

4.7.1.en: At the first: that is, his first visit to Galatia.

4.7.3.en: As an angel of God: you honored me as an angel sent from God.

4.7.4.en: Paul testifies that he suffered from illnesses in his body when he visited and preached in Galatia, and that the Galatians were not troubled by his bodily weakness nor did they despise him, but on the contrary they felt that he was like an angel whom God had sent to them and an image of Christ, for they saw Christ in him, so they honored him greatly.

4.8.0.en: The blessedness ye spake of: the praise you received from others because of your strong love for me.

4.8.1.en: Paul asks about the Galatians' strong love for him, for which everyone praises them: where has it gone, and how did they turn against him because he rebuked them for believing that the Law is a condition for receiving salvation, as the false teachers claimed? At the same time he encourages them by testifying to their intense love for him, and that they would have wished, if possible, to pluck out their eyes and give them to him so that he could see with them. It is understood that his temptation was the weakness of his eyesight, as proved by the fact that he used to dictate his epistles to one of his disciples, as is mentioned at the end of each epistle. This epistle, however, he wrote himself, but in large letters (ch. 6:11). This may support the opinion of some who say that this epistle was written early, before the other epistles, when his sight was better than afterward.

4.9.0.en: Because I tell you the truth: I declared that your acceptance of the teaching of the false teachers separates you from Christ and you return to Judaism.

4.9.1.en: Paul is astonished at the change in the Galatians from intense love for him to enmity toward him, because he was frank with them and declared to them their error in accepting the false teachers.

4.10.0.en: They zealously affect you: the false teachers show their love for the Galatians so that they follow them in their mistaken teachings.

4.10.1.en: Exclude you: draw you away from true faith in Christ.

4.10.2.en: Ye might affect them: you love them and become attached to their differing teachings.

4.10.3.en: Paul warns the Galatians of the deceit of the false teachers in their self-serving love for them, in order to gain followers of their mistaken ideas. This love is evil and draws them away from the truth, so that they become attached to these teachers and follow them in their deviations.

4.11.0.en: Paul praises the people's love for their teachers and their obedience to them, but in sound and good teachings and not false teachings. The Galatians loved Paul and obeyed his message when he visited them, so would that they remain firm in this faith in Christ and in their love for him.

4.12.0.en: Paul speaks in a spirit of fatherhood toward the Galatians and likens himself to the mother who suffers the pains of childbirth (labor). He bears their fickleness and tries to bring them back to sound faith so that he may bring them forth as children of Christ and a true image of Him.

4.13.0.en: To change my voice: to speak with kindness and encouragement instead of the rebuke that I wrote in this epistle.

4.13.1.en: I stand in doubt of you: I do not know whether you have been convinced by the proofs I have given, or whether it is better to rebuke you firmly or encourage you gently so that you return to the faith safe.

4.13.2.en: Paul wishes to visit Galatia to know how its people respond to his message, and to show his fatherhood with words of tenderness and encouragement in order to win them for Christ. He is ready to rebuke them, convince them and encourage them, that is, to use every way to bring them back to their first faith in Christ.

4.13.3.en: Praise the behavior of those around you so that you win their love and encourage them to accept your guidance that binds them to Christ, because if they are at ease with you and love you they will obey your teachings and be attached to the Church.

4.14.s.en: (4) A comparison between the seed of Sarah and of Hagar

4.14.0.en: The law: the five books of Moses.

4.14.1.en: St. Paul says to the Galatians: If you do not want to listen to the Gospel, then go back to our father Abraham, in whom the Jews boast as their greatest father. He compares at length Hagar the bondwoman, whose name means Sinai, who emigrated to the wilderness of Sinai, and whose offspring was a symbol of the bondage under the Law and the heirs of the earthly Jerusalem, and Sarah the free woman, whose name means princess and mother of many, and whose offspring is a symbol of the freedom that is in Christ and the heirs of the heavenly Jerusalem. Ishmael is the son of the flesh according to fleshly counsel, and Hagar represents the covenant of the Law which God gave to the children of Israel on Mount Sinai in the Arabian desert, which is the land of Hagar's descendants. All her children were born into bondage, and the covenant was conditional on obedience: "Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me" (Ex 19:5). The Jews used to boast that they were children of Abraham and had never been in bondage to anyone, so the Apostle Paul told them that everyone who returns to be enslaved to the Law is a son of Hagar and a son of the earthly Jerusalem, and is a captive to the rulings and ordinances of the Law, and remains a slave who does not inherit.

4.15.0.en: Paul declares that he is using the wives of Abraham, Hagar and Sarah, as a representation and symbol of those who are subject to the Law, that is, the Jews, and of those who enjoy faith, that is, the Christians. He distinguishes between them by saying "two covenants": the first, which Hagar signifies, is the one made on Mount Sinai, because the meaning of the word Hagar is Sinai, as the ancient Arabs called it, and on this mountain Moses received the Law to which the Jews cling, and whose capital in the time of the Apostle Paul was Jerusalem. Paul affirms that the Jews are enslaved to the Law, which reveals only the faults of man, and have not yet received the freedom of the children of God through their Christian faith.

4.16.0.en: Jerusalem which is above: he means the Church of the New Testament, the Christian Church, which is higher and loftier than the Law, that is, the earthly Jerusalem, and the goal of the Christian Church is the heavenly Jerusalem. The mother of us all: the Christian Church is the mother of all believers, and it is signified by Sarah, who is the mother of all believers through her son Isaac.

4.16.1.en: Free: Sarah is the free lady and not a bondwoman, and her children are the believers in Christ, whom He freed from the death of sin and the bondage of the Law, which sentences them to death because they are sinners, since Christ accomplished redemption by His death on their behalf and gave them the new, free life in Him.

4.16.2.en: The Apostle makes clear that the Church, the mother of all believers, is free from the chains of the Law.

4.17.0.en: Thou barren .. thou that travailest not: he means Sarah, who signifies the Gentiles far from the faith, who had no fruit of life with God.

4.17.1.en: The children of the desolate: the children of Sarah by faith, that is, the Gentiles.

4.17.2.en: Her which hath an husband: the children of Hagar, by whom he means the Jews enslaved to the Law, because Hagar, as we mentioned, signifies Mount Sinai on which Moses received the Law.

4.17.3.en: Paul cites the prophet Isaiah (Isa 54:1), who speaks about Jerusalem forsaken in the days of the captivity, but it would be rebuilt and its sons would return from the captivity.

4.17.4.en: The same prophecy is about the Gentiles far from God, who will believe in the Christian Church and become the majority in it. So Isaiah says, "Rejoice, thou barren" who was formerly barren (Sarah), which signifies the Church of the Gentiles, while she "which hath an husband" signifies the Jews.

4.18.1.en: We, as Christians, are children of promise, born by faith from the font of Baptism, which is the womb of the Church our mother, born from above by our faith in God's promise of redemption, and we return to our free mother, the heavenly Jerusalem, because everyone who believed and acted by the faith of Abraham and Sarah became a son of Abraham, as Isaac was, the son of promise.

4.19.0.en: Born after the flesh: he is Ishmael, who signifies the Jews who live by the fleshly ordinances of the Law.

4.19.1.en: After the Spirit: he is Isaac, who signifies the Christian Church, most of which is of Gentile origin. At the weaning of Isaac his parents made a feast, and Sarah saw the son of the bondwoman mocking, and it is said that he was aiming his arrows at Isaac, threatening to kill him as a way of frightening him (Gen 21:9). This is an example of the Jews' persecution of the Christians.

4.20.0.en: Sarah said to Abraham, cast out the bondwoman, for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the free woman (Gen 21:10), and the Lord said to him, listen to all that Sarah has said to you. For the inheritance is only for the sons born from above: "Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God" (Jn 3:3). It means that there can be no agreement between the Jews who insist that the Law is a condition for salvation and the true believers who know that salvation is by the blood of Christ alone. Therefore the false teachers, that is, the Christians of Jewish origin who try to bring Christianity back to Judaism by submitting to the Law, have no share in the Church.

4.21.0.en: In conclusion, the Apostle Paul sums up the position of the believers in the Christian Church: they are the children of Sarah the free woman, that is, the children of faith in Christ, who frees them from the bondage of sin, and not the children of the bondwoman Hagar, that is, those subject to the Law with its ordinances, which reveal man's weakness and do not save him. So he rejects clinging to the Law after faith in Christ.

4.21.1.en: Let us hold fast to the work of grace in our lives and struggle by it to overcome the bad habits that dominate us, confident of God's power however repeated or hard our sins may be, and our confidence in the new life that God has given us urges us to quick repentance, to holding fast to the Church and to doing good. Christian freedom
